newsitem.title: CHINA: China say disputed oil rig's action irreproachable.
newsitem.headline: China say disputed oil rig's action irreproachable.

text.p: Beijing government and oil officials on Thursday defended Chinese oil exploration in disputed waters near Vietnam, saying drilling in the area was irreproachable and China had no plans to withdraw.
In Vietnam, a Foreign Ministry spokesman restated Hanoi's claim to the area where the Chinese Kan Tan III rig has sparked a diplomatic crisis by drilling exploratory oil wells.

China cherished its ties with its southern communist neighbour and was willing to hold talks to resolve outstanding problems, but the actions of its rig were beyond criticism, said Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai.

"It is irreproachable for China's Kan Tan III rig to carry out normal operations in the north part of the South China Sea on China's declared continental shelf and exclusive economic zone," Cui told a news briefing in Beijing.
An official of China's main offshore oil company said it had no immediate plans to move the rig from the disputed area, about 64.5 nautical miles off the coast of mainland central Vietnam.
"Any decision to leave the drilling area would be based on the drilling results," the China National Offshore Oil Corp official told Reuters.
"Why should we leave the area?" said the official. "When the exploration is finished we will move the rig."
The Chinese comments were in stark contrast to repeated demands from Hanoi for an immediate withdrawal from the area.

"As we have made clear, the area where the Chinese oil rig Kan Tan 111 is operating is completely located in the special economic zone and continental shelf of Vietnam," a Vietnamese Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
"... we have requested that experts from the two countries meet as soon as possible, at any place, to discuss this. We hope that China will positively respond to this request," he said.
The oil exploration dispute is the latest in a long series of territorial disputes, ideological differences and historical grievances to strain the socialist solidarity between China and Vietnam.

The communist neighbours, which contest parts of their land frontier as well as large swathes of the resource-rich South China Sea, fought a brief but bloody border war in 1979 and clashed offshore in the 1980s.

Both sides have in recent years agreed to shelve some border problems and have worked to improve ties and boost trade, but the temptation to exploit the mineral wealth under the disputed waters has been a constant threat to their rapprochement.
